Comment: Absolutive is unmarked (-Ø) in Matis. Both S and O bear no case marker. Ergative A is marked with -n.
Matis 1st person singular pronouns follow ergative alignment: A=embi, S/O=ebi. The 1+2 inclusive nuki/muki is neutral (invariant).

Matis 2nd person singular follows ergative alignment (A=mimbi, S/O=mibi), but 2nd person plural follows ACCUSATIVE alignment: mikui in A/S position, mitso in O position. So there is a singular/plural split: singular=ergative, plural=accusative.

Matis 3rd person singular non-emphatic is Ø (neutral). 3rd person plural non-emphatic: Ø in A/S, ato in O — accusative alignment. 4th person (emphatic/coreferential): akui in A/S, ato in O — accusative alignment. Overall, 3rd person pronouns do NOT follow ergative alignment.
Full NPs in Matis follow strict ergative-absolutive case marking: A marked with -n (ERG), S and O unmarked (-Ø, ABS). See ex. (1a,b): dëndu-n 'electric.eel-ERG', tumi-Ø 'man's.name-ABS'.

No aspect-based split documented. Fleck explicitly states: 'there are no typical split alignment systems in Mayoruna languages, such as splits conditioned by tense/aspect/mood' (p. 35). Ergative alignment applies regardless of aspect.
No aspect-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in perfective contexts. Ex. (1a) uses immediate past inflection with ergative A.
No tense-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in past tense. Ex. (1a): dëndu-n tumi-Ø pëdka-a-sh 'electric.eel-ERG man's.name-ABS shock-IMM.PAST-3'.
No tense-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in non-past. Ex. (25a): ëmbi du-Ø pe-e-k '1ERG howler.monkey-ABS eat-NPAST-INDIC'.
No mood-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in indicative mood.
No mood-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in non-indicative moods.
No realis/irrealis split documented. Ergative alignment applies in realis contexts.
No realis/irrealis split documented. Ergative alignment applies in irrealis contexts.
No agentivity-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies with agentive A. Extended intransitive verbs (§4) are an exception at the verb-class level, not agentivity-based.

Psych-verbs and experiencer verbs in Matis are treated as transitive with the Experiencer in ergative case (p. 48). E.g. dais 'desire, covet' takes ERG Experiencer. Ergative applies with non-agentive A.
No topicality-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies regardless of topicality of A.
No topicality-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies regardless of topicality of A.
No animacy-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies with animate A.
No animacy-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies with inanimate A.
Ergative alignment is documented in main clauses. This is the primary context described.

Ergative alignment has been extended to reanalyzed negative constructions (§6.1) AND abilitative constructions (§6.2) in Matis. Ex. (25b): ëmbi du-Ø pe-emen(-pa) ik-e-k '1ERG howler.monkey-ABS eat-NEG AUX-NPAST-INDIC'. Ex. (31b): dabi-n du-Ø pe-tepad 'David-ERG howler.monkey-ABS eat-ABIL'. Matis is further along in ergativizing these constructions than Matses.

Yes, two conditioning factors: (1) VERB CLASS: extended intransitive verbs (bëama 'forget', cho 'have') take two ABS arguments. (2) NOMINAL CLASS/NUMBER: singular pronouns (1sg, 2sg, 3sg emphatic) are ergative; 1+2 inclusive nuki/muki is neutral; 2pl and 3pl pronouns follow ACCUSATIVE alignment (mikui/miki in A/S, mitso in O; akui in A/S, ato in O). This is a three-way ergative-neutral-accusative split in the pronoun system.

Yes. On full nouns, ergative case is marked identically to genitive and instrumental: -n (with allomorph -ën after consonants). Note: on pronouns, ergative and genitive differ in form (e.g. 1sg ERG=embi, GEN=nukun).

Yes for instrumental: on full nouns, ergative and instrumental are both marked with -n. Comitative is expressed by a distinct postposition: -bëd 'Comitative' (p. 37). So: ergative = instrumental (same marker -n), but ergative ≠ comitative.
